header.title: OpsAPI
header.subtitle: One API for sign-in, tenants and business modules.
header.description: OpsAPI is a self-hosted, multi-tenant API platform. It signs your users in once for every app, keeps each customer's data in its own workspace, and switches on the business modules a product needs, from CRM to UK tax filing. Open source, built on OpenResty, Lua and PostgreSQL.

intro.title: Stop building a backend per product
intro.body: Every product rebuilds the same four things: sign-in, tenants, the business logic and the operations around them. OpsAPI does them once. Lua runs inside OpenResty's Nginx workers, so a request never hops to a separate app server, and each deployment loads only the modules its preset names. It is the platform behind TenthMatrix applications such as AI Tax Filing, and it is open source on GitHub, built and run by Workstation, TenthMatrix's sister brand.

pillars.title: Four things every product rebuilds, done once

items.title: One sign-in for every app
items.text: Passwords with emailed codes, Google and Apple, SAML single sign-on per workspace, and a hosted sign-in page. Apps check a token with one call to /auth/me.

items.title: Workspaces from the first table
items.text: Every business row carries its workspace. Roles are module.action permissions per workspace, so one deployment serves many customers without their data mixing.

items.title: 20 business modules
items.text: CRM, invoicing, accounting, UK tax filing, e-commerce, care, field service and more. Each deployment loads only what its product uses.

items.title: Built to be run
items.text: One container, a Helm chart, secrets from a vault, health checks, Prometheus metrics and an error catalogue with correlation IDs.

architecture.title: Lua inside Nginx, PostgreSQL underneath
architecture.intro: OpsAPI is a Lapis application that runs inside OpenResty's Nginx workers. A minimal deployment needs only PostgreSQL; Redis, MinIO, Kafka and an AI model are optional.

steps.title: Clients
steps.text: The admin dashboard, your web and mobile apps, servers and scripts, all on the same API and the same sign-in.

steps.title: OpenResty workers
steps.text: Lua runs in the Nginx worker processes: no proxy hop and no separate app server.

steps.title: Modules per deployment
steps.text: The PROJECT_CODE preset decides which modules load. A module that is not loaded has no routes and no tables.

steps.title: 服务
steps.text: PostgreSQL with pgvector for every table, plus optional Redis, MinIO or S3, Kafka, Ollama or a hosted model, and Prometheus.

howItWorks.title: One request through OpsAPI
howItWorks.intro: Every request follows the same layered path, from the Nginx worker to PostgreSQL.

flow.title: 1. Before filter
flow.text: Public endpoints are let through; everything else needs a valid token or API key.

flow.title: 2. Middleware
flow.text: The workspace is resolved from a header, the token or the subdomain, and the caller's module.action permission is checked.

flow.title: 3. Routes
flow.text: Only the route files for the modules this deployment loads exist.

flow.title: 4. Queries
flow.text: Business logic, validation and SQL, always filtered by workspace.

flow.title: 5. Models and PostgreSQL
flow.text: Thin table wrappers over one database per deployment, with workspaces separating the tenants.

aiAngle.title: Sign-in and security, built in
aiAngle.intro: The parts every product needs and few get right are always on, in every deployment.
points: Email and password with bcrypt, lockout after failed attempts, per-IP rate limits, and reset links only to trusted origins.
Six-digit codes by email. Each workspace owner decides whether members need one; platform admins always do.
Google and Sign in with Apple on web and native apps, and SAML 2.0 single sign-on per workspace with Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, OneLogin or Keycloak.
Rotating refresh tokens, an optional PIN for quick unlock, and API keys scoped to one workspace for servers and scripts.
A per-workspace audit trail, and an error catalogue where every error has a code, a plain message and a correlation ID.

roadmap.title: Pick the modules per deployment
roadmap.intro: Choose one preset with PROJECT_CODE, or combine them, for example ecommerce,collaboration. Sign-in, workspaces and roles are always included. There are 16 presets in all.

deploy.title: From one command to a Kubernetes cluster
deploy.body: Pull bwalia/opsapi from Docker Hub, or clone the repository and run ./start.sh -e local -n -j all to bring up the API, dashboard, PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Kafka, Grafana and Prometheus. For production, the Helm chart runs migrations before each upgrade, takes secrets from a vault and rolls updates with a graceful drain. The @opsapi/client TypeScript SDK and the OpenAPI spec at /openapi.json cover every endpoint.

items.question: Is OpsAPI open source?
items.answer: Yes. The code is on GitHub at bwalia/opsapi and the image is on Docker Hub. You run it on your own infrastructure.

items.question: What does a minimal deployment need?
items.answer: One container and PostgreSQL. Redis, MinIO or S3, Kafka, an AI model and Prometheus are optional and only needed by the modules and features that use them.

items.question: Can one customer be limited to certain modules?
items.answer: The hard boundary is the deployment: a deployment's preset decides which modules exist, and a module that is not loaded returns 404 for everyone. Within a deployment, roles control what each member can do in their workspace.

items.question: Can I add my own module without forking it?
items.answer: Yes. A plugin is a folder of Lua that gets sign-in, workspaces, permissions, migrations, dashboard pages, event listeners and scheduled jobs, and ships in its own image built on bwalia/opsapi.

items.question: Can TenthMatrix run it for us?
items.answer: Yes. TenthMatrix builds products on OpsAPI and can set it up on your cloud or your own servers, add the modules and integrations you need, and keep it running.
